---
title: "Predicting Reported Cyber Incident Losses in Financial Institutions"
author: "Fernanda Lopez, Emiliano Santacruz, and Aidee Mendez"
---

## Research question

To what extent do incident type, institution size, and event year help predict reported economic losses from cyber incidents at financial institutions?

Our audience is risk management and cybersecurity teams at financial institutions. We want to understand which incident characteristics help explain differences in reported losses.

## Data source

We use the [VERIS Community Database (VCDB)](https://github.com/vz-risk/VCDB/tree/f6f98c00f66ab35f5b49977a5852ce94a5bb31d1). Each row is one incident. The response is reported loss in USD. Predictors are incident type, employee-count category, and incident year.

The code below embeds 61 finance-and-insurance records with positive reported losses. Keeping USD records with known size and year, and excluding a security-budget amount and an unrelated fine, leaves 26 incidents. Public reports are not a random sample, and missing losses are not zero.

The embedded data are adapted from VCDB under [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). No customer or employee identifiers are included. The code contains the data and preparation steps needed to reproduce the baseline.

```{r}
                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                          na.strings = c("", "Unknown"))

usd <- subset(loss_snapshot, !is.na(currency) & currency == "USD")
complete <- usd[complete.cases(usd[c("year", "employee_count")]), ]
excluded_ids <- c(
  "F61D6C46-14A7-42B2-8AD4-3808270BF631", # Annual security budget.
  "2B6947F8-AFFA-41D2-9140-CC67CCC2FC9A"  # Fine unrelated to disclosure.
)
analysis <- complete[!complete$incident_id %in% excluded_ids, ]

small_codes <- c("1 to 10", "11 to 100", "101 to 1000", "Small")
analysis$size <- factor(
  ifelse(analysis$employee_count %in% small_codes,
         "Up to 1,000", "Over 1,000"),
  levels = c("Up to 1,000", "Over 1,000")
)
analysis$type <- factor(
  ifelse(analysis$hacking == 1 | analysis$malware == 1,
         "Hacking or malware",
         ifelse(analysis$misuse == 1 | analysis$social == 1,
                "Misuse or social", "Physical or error")),
  levels = c("Physical or error", "Misuse or social", "Hacking or malware")
)
analysis$year_c <- analysis$year - 2013
analysis$log_loss <- log(analysis$loss_amount)

stopifnot(nrow(loss_snapshot) == 61, ncol(loss_snapshot) == 11,
          nrow(usd) == 35, nrow(complete) == 28, nrow(analysis) == 26,
          !anyDuplicated(analysis$incident_id),
          all(is.finite(analysis$log_loss)))

knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Check = c("Embedded loss records", "Source fields", "USD records",
            "Complete USD records", "Final analysis records",
            "Up to 1,000 employees", "Over 1,000 employees"),
  Value = c(nrow(loss_snapshot), ncol(loss_snapshot), nrow(usd),
            nrow(complete), nrow(analysis),
            sum(analysis$size == "Up to 1,000"),
            sum(analysis$size == "Over 1,000"))
), align = c("l", "r"))
```

```{r}
#| include: false
baseline <- lm(log_loss ~ type + size + year_c, data = analysis)
```

## Baseline

Our baseline predicts natural log loss from incident type, institution size, and year. Its R-squared is 0.260. The estimated loss ratio for larger versus smaller institutions is 12.0, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.28 to 521.5. Only five incidents involve smaller institutions, so the comparison is uncertain.
